record.paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
record.original_question: For ternary patterns in partial-word avoidability, where ternary patterns are patterns over the three variables alpha, beta, and gamma, determine the avoidability indices of such patterns, or at least bounds for those indices; also determine a bound on the length of unavoidable ternary patterns.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A partial word over a finite alphabet A is a sequence whose entries are either letters of A or a distinguished "hole" symbol ⋄ (which is compatible with every letter). A pattern p is a (full) word over a pattern alphabet E = {α, β, γ, …} of variables. A pattern p is said to be k-avoidable in partial words if there exists an infinite partial word w over some alphabet of size k such that no factor of w is a "partial-word instance" of p, where a partial-word instance is obtained by applying a non-erasing morphism h: E* → A* (assigning to each variable a nonempty full word) and then allowing some positions of the resulting word to be replaced by ⋄ provided each occurrence pattern is preserved up to compatibility. The partial-word avoidability index μ_p(p) is the least integer k ≥ 1 such that p is k-avoidable in partial words (and ∞ if no such k exists, in which case p is called unavoidable in partial words).

Restrict attention to ternary patterns, i.e., patterns over exactly three variables {α, β, γ}.

Problems.
(a) For every ternary pattern p, determine the partial-word avoidability index μ_p(p), or, failing that, give nontrivial upper and lower bounds for μ_p(p).
(b) Determine an explicit bound L such that every ternary pattern of length greater than L is avoidable in partial words (equivalently, bound the length of the longest unavoidable ternary patterns).
artifact.status_search_result: The partial-word avoidability indices of ternary patterns have been computed for most cases by Blanchet-Sadri and collaborators, who classified ternary patterns by index (with 4 patterns of index 5, 24 of index 4, and 209–216 of index 3). However, the indices of a small set of ternary patterns (e.g., αβαγβγ, ααβγγαβ, ααβαγαββα, αββαγααβα) remain undetermined, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Computing the Partial Word Avoidability Indices of Ternary Patterns
status_evidence.snippet: Among ternary patterns, there are 4 with avoidability index 5, 24 with index 4, between 209 and 216 with index 3, and the rest have index 2.
status_evidence.claim: Indices of ternary patterns are largely classified but a small set remains with only bounds.

status_evidence.title: Pattern avoidance in partial words over a ternary alphabet
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem involves finding avoidability indices for ternary patterns αβαγβγ, ααβγγαβ, ααβαγαββα, αββαγααβα.
status_evidence.claim: Several specific ternary patterns still have undetermined partial-word avoidability index.
